actions.action: Remove the plant from its pot and clean all the old soil off the roots
Soak the plant in a hydrogen peroxide solution (1 tsp 3% per 1.5 L water) for about 30 minutes
Keep the bare-root plant in a container of plain water for about a month
Cut off the top part and try to root it in water
Repot into peat-based soil with perlite, optionally with expanded clay at the bottom, without burying the stem too deep
Give the first watering with a hydrogen peroxide solution (1 tsp per liter)
Check the topsoil with a finger and water only when it is dry

verdict.reason: The answer never identifies overgrowth or legginess and says the cause doesn't matter. Its main advice is to bare-root the plant, soak it in peroxide and keep it in water for a month, with only an incidental top cutting, so the hard trim is buried. Stripping the roots and water-culturing a plant that only needed a trim is unnecessary stress that delays the real fix.
